current_round.prompt:
From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: State-sync: disjoint per-node nodes.json fork becomes an unrecoverable hard conflict when the merge baseline is missing (needs manual state-recovery)

Body:
Subject: State-sync: disjoint per-node nodes.json fork becomes an unrecoverable hard conflict when the merge baseline is missing (needs manual state-recovery)

Severity: High �X halts all-node state synchronization; dashboard shows "counts are non-authoritative"; requires manual
operator recovery.

Environment
- Target app: /insurity/ProSuite, node bo2lnxnevo03-buddy, runtime root /insurity/refine/run/8082.
- Build: bin/refine deployed 2026-08-17 09:27 (the release that added the state_sync_stale_threshold_seconds default
and dropped worktree_cleanup_generated_paths).
- Fleet: 5 registered nodes; at time of incident only this node was live.

Symptom
Dashboard banner: "State sync has failed since 2026-08-17T11:58:56Z. All-node counts are local and non-authoritative
until synchronization recovers." Health record: status: failed, last_error: "Refine state changed on multiple nodes
during first_pass: 1 unresolved path(s)", unresolved_paths: ["nodes.json"].

What triggered it
The 09:27 release performs a settings-schema migration. On first load+save after deploy, each node normalized its own
nodes.json entry (added state_sync_stale_threshold_seconds, removed worktree_cleanup_generated_paths). This node's
entry migrated at 11:29; the QA node (default) migrated at 11:28. Each side changed only its own record from a shared
pre-migration base �X i.e. a disjoint, per-node divergence.

Expected
merge_node_registry (src/tools/host/git_sync/node_registry_merge.rs:18) is explicitly built for this: last-writer-wins
per node id, retaining one-sided changes. The disjoint case is covered by the
disjoint_heartbeat_updates_merge_by_node_id unit test. It should have auto-resolved with no operator involvement.

Actual �X root cause
In prepare_semantic_state_changes (src/tools/host/git_sync/service.rs:426�V455), the merge only runs if the
common-ancestor bytes can be loaded:

let Some(base_bytes) = self.load_baseline_file(state_root, &relative, *base_fingerprint)? else {
  continue;   // baseline unrecoverable -> path left unresolved -> hard conflict
};
...
let Some(merged) = merged else { continue; };

load_baseline_file (state_worktree.rs:296�V315) recovers the base content by scanning refine/state history for a
revision whose content matches the stored fingerprint. If that fingerprint's bytes are not reachable in history �X or
the baseline fingerprint file (.git/refine-state-baseline.json) is stale/absent �X it returns None, the merge is
silently skipped via continue, and nodes.json is reported as an unresolved first_pass conflict.

Net effect: a fork the semantic merge is designed to resolve becomes a hard, sync-blocking conflict, solely because
the base couldn't be reconstructed. On this host the baseline file was dated 10:12 (stale relative to the 11:28/11:29
migration), consistent with this path. We suspect the baseline went stale/missing around the earlier runtime-root
migration (two runtime roots have bitten us before).

Contributing issue #1 �X silent skip, no diagnostic
When load_baseline_file returns None, there's no log/telemetry distinguishing "genuine multi-writer conflict" from
"couldn't reconstruct base, so I gave up." Operators can't tell a real conflict from a recoverable-but-skipped one.

Contributing issue #2 �X recovery preview is unusable while automation runs
Each failed sync attempt appends a state_sync activity entry into live .refine state (see append_state_sync_activity),
which mutates the live snapshot. state-recovery preview fences on a stable live snapshot and aborts with "the live
state snapshot changed" (recovery/service.rs:141,200). Because the failing sync loop writes on every attempt, preview
fails every time until automation is paused. We observed 3/3 preview failures back-to-back; it only succeeded after
refine workflow pause. The recovery tool the error message tells you to run doesn't work in the state it's advertised
for.

Contributing issue #3 �X no backoff on a persistent conflict (amplifies #2)
On a non-transient conflict the sync worker keeps retrying at the debounce cadence (state_sync_debounce_seconds,
default 5s; schedule.rs) with no failure backoff. attempt_sequence advanced ~1000 (22512 �� 23542) in minutes, each
attempt re-appending activity-log churn. This both spams the activity log and sustains the snapshot churn in #2.
(Related to the still-pending backoff/GC work noted from the earlier claims-bloat incident.)

Impact on multi-node recovery (why this matters now)
Three nodes are currently shut down and will restart on the new binary. On startup each will re-migrate its own
nodes.json entry (self-update) while its local refine/state is behind origin �X the same disjoint per-node divergence.
They should auto-merge on their first project sync only if their baseline is intact and the base bytes are reachable
in refine/state history. Any node whose baseline went stale (same runtime-root history as this one) will reproduce
this hard conflict on startup and need manual state-recovery. A raw git pull is not a safe substitute �X it invokes
git's line-level merge on nodes.json instead of the semantic per-node merge and can leave the worktree conflicted.

Workaround that resolved it (for reference)
1. refine workflow pause (stops the failing-sync churn so preview can get a stable snapshot).
2. refine project state-recovery preview �� apply --authority remote (QA treated as authoritative for the registry).
3. refine project sync (settles health, refreshes baseline, re-normalizes this node's entry, pushes to origin).
4. refine workflow resume.
Post-fix: last_attempt_outcome: succeeded, all failure/stale/error fields cleared; both migrated node entries
identical on live and remote.

Suggested fixes for dev to consider
1. When load_baseline_file returns None for a disjoint per-node change, fall back to a base-less 2-way per-node
reconcile (LWW by updated_at) instead of continue, or at minimum emit a distinct, logged outcome ("merge skipped: base
unrecoverable") rather than a generic hard conflict.
2. Make state-recovery preview/apply resilient to the sync worker's own activity-log writes �X e.g. exclude state_sync
activity appends from the stale-fence snapshot, or auto-quiesce sync for the duration of a preview, so recovery works
without a manual pause.
3. Add failure backoff to the sync scheduler so a persistent conflict doesn't retry every ~5s indefinitely and
self-amplify via activity-log churn.
4. Investigate why the baseline (.git/refine-state-baseline.json) went stale/unrecoverable �X likely tied to the
runtime-root migration; ensure save_state_baseline runs (and history retains the fingerprinted bytes) across
runtime-root moves.

Artifacts available on request: conflict report run/8082/state-sync-conflicts/latest.json, health record
run/8082/state-sync-health.json, recovery manifest under ProSuite/.git/refine-state-recoveries/.
